summary: Join our training course on risk management in rural development projects. Learn essential techniques to mitigate risks and drive successful outcomes.
lede: Risk management in rural development projects involves identifying root causes, stakeholders, assumptions, and external factors that may affect an intervention. For rural project professionals designing or reviewing proposals, the course develops skills in assessing local needs, building logframes with indicators and assumptions, and aligning activities, timelines, and budgets with project objectives.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for professionals who are actively involved in designing projects and writing or reviewing proposals for rural development.
audience: Government staff in rural development, agriculture
Leaders of farmer organizations, cooperatives, and producer
Staff of faith-based and community-based organizations
Technical specialists (agriculture, livelihoods, WASH, health, education)
modules: Rural Development Context and Project Thinking
Defining Objectives, Results, and Theory of Change
Designing the Logical Framework for Rural Projects
Budgeting and Resource Planning for Rural Projects
Cross Cutting Issues in Rural Project Design
Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning in Project Design
Writing the Proposal: From Concept to Full Application
Reviewing, Refining, and Presenting Your Proposal
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of rural development concepts and some experience in project design or proposal writing.
